propositions: Four ast.parse/inspect.getsource guards silently pass unconditionally because they scan hardcoded source files that no longer contain the policed constructs after sibling module refactors (findings 1–4: applier invariants import, llm timeout handlers, inbound_probe adapter imports, usage_log string parsing).
Vacuous guards lack anti-vacuity assertions that verify the scanned population is non-empty and semantically covers the actual construct location, allowing silent failures when code relocates.

Two additional guards (findings 5, 7, 8) are at-risk or misdiagnosed: capabilities.py lacks a landmark assertion, jira/backend.py's mutating-member list misses unscanned transport modules, and passes.py triggering is a false positive substring match.

The repair pattern proven on bug 34c2 applies: derive scan population programmatically rather than hardcode file names, add explicit landmark/coverage assertions, and validate with mutation tests that re-introduce the construct at its real home.
Finding 6's relative pathlib.Path guard breaks when pytest runs outside the repo root (working directory dependency not anchored to __file__).

All four confirmed vacuous guards (F1–F4) and borderline F5 require repairs with measurement-backed anti-vacuity assertions; F6 requires relative-path anchoring; F7–F8 require explicit disposition (accepted vs. fixed).
